Should it become necessary to dredge within herring spawning habitat and outside of the herring work window (March 16th to November 30th of any year), the USACE shall implement the following measures:
A CDFW qualified and trained herring observer shall be present during all dredging or in-water work (day and night) and observing shall be his/her sole duty.
The herring observer shall monitor for herring spawn in 500-meter buffer zone surrounding active dredging and disposal activities.
Observations may be conducted from the dredge, shore, or by a separate vessel, but must have a full view of the buffer zone around the dredging activity;

When there is a lag time of eight hours or more between dredging activities and following dredging at night, the herring observer shall conduct a shoreline survey within the 500-meter buffer zone at least one hour prior to the start of dredging;
If spawning Pacific herring are detected within 500 meters of the dredging site all in- water work shall stop immediately and Commission staff and CDFW shall be notified.
The observer shall keep a daily log of observations, which shall be submitted to Commission staff and the CDFW on a weekly basis by 5:00 pm on Fridays;

(a) If required to determine that a prospective contractor is responsible, the offeror must:
1) Demonstrate that they have adequate financial resources to perform the contract or the ability to obtain them.
2) Be able to comply with the required or proposed delivery or perform schedule, taking into consideration all
existing commercial and governmental business commitments.
3) Have a satisfactory performance record. In making the determination of responsibility, the Government
Contracting Officer shall consider relevant past performance information. A prospective contractor shall not be
determined as responsible or not responsible solely based on a lack of relevant performance history except when
there are special standards set forth in the solicitation, which applies, to all offerors that must be met in order to
receive the award. These special standards may be necessary when unusual expertise or specialized facilities are
necessary in the performance of the contract; therefore, in order to be determined as responsible for a particular
contract, the offeror must be able to meet those special standards. A prospective contractor that is or recently has
been seriously deficient in contract performance shall be presumed to be nonresponsive unless the Contracting
Officer determines that the circumstances were beyond the contractor's control or that the contractor has taken
appropriate corrective action. Other responsibility considerations by the Contracting Officer will include past efforts
by the contractor to apply sufficient tenacity and perseverance to perform acceptably, to meet quality requirements
of contracts, and the contractor's past compliance with subcontracting plans (if required) under recent contracts.
4) Have a satisfactory record of integrity and business ethics.
5) Have the necessary organization, experience, accounting and operational controls, and technical skills, or the
ability to obtain them (including, as appropriate, such elements as production control procedures, property control
systems, quality assurance measures, and safety programs applicable to materials to be produced or services to be SOLICITATION
performed by the prospective contractor and subcontractors).
6) Have the necessary production, construction, and technical equipment and facilities, or the ability to obtain them.
7) Be otherwise qualified and eligible to receive an award under applicable laws and regulations.
rows.normalized: The offeror must satisfy the seven listed responsibility criteria (financial resources, delivery/performance schedule capability, satisfactory performance record, integrity, organization/technical skills, production/technical facilities, legal eligibility) when required for a responsibility determination.

A brief description of each specific plan required by environmental SOLICITATION

site who oversee environmental compliance, such as who is responsible for

responsible for training the Contractor's environmental protection

rows.verbatim:
Reimburse the
Government for costs incurred including sample analysis materials,
clothing, equipment, and labor if the Government will initiate its own
spill cleanup procedures, for Contractor-responsible spills, when: Spill
cleanup procedures have not begun within one hour of spill
discovery/occurrence; or, in the Government's judgment, spill cleanup is
inadequate and the spill remains a threat to human health or the
environment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must reimburse Government costs if Government must initiate its own cleanup for contractor-responsible spills under specified conditions.

rows.verbatim:
Immediately report to the Governmental instances of breakage or mercury
spillage.
rows.normalized: Contractor must immediately report breakage or mercury spillage to the Government.

rows.verbatim: Clean mercury spill area to the satisfaction of the Government.
rows.normalized: Contractor must clean mercury spill area to Government's satisfaction.

rows.verbatim:
Do not recycle a mercury spill cleanup; manage it as a hazardous waste for
disposal.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not recycle mercury spill cleanup and must manage it as hazardous waste for disposal.

rows.verbatim:
Clean previously used equipment prior to bringing it onto the project
site.
rows.normalized: Contractor must clean previously used equipment before bringing it onto the project site.

rows.verbatim:
Equipment must be free from soil residuals, egg deposits from plant
pests, noxious weeds, and plant seeds.
rows.normalized: Equipment must be free of soil residuals, pest egg deposits, noxious weeds, and plant seeds.

rows.verbatim:
Consult with the U.S. Department of Agriculture jurisdictional office for
additional cleaning requirements.
rows.normalized: Contractor must consult USDA jurisdictional office for additional cleaning requirements.

rows.verbatim: Manage and dispose of contaminated waste in accordance with 40 CFR 761.
rows.normalized: Contractor must manage and dispose of PCB-contaminated waste per 40 CFR 761.

rows.verbatim:
In the event military munitions, as defined in 40 CFR 260, are discovered
or uncovered, immediately stop work in that area and immediately inform
the Government.
rows.normalized: If military munitions are discovered, contractor must immediately stop work in that area and inform the Government.

rows.verbatim:
Store POL products and fuel equipment and motor vehicles in
a manner that affords the maximum protection against spills into the
environment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must store POL products and fuel equipment/vehicles to maximize spill protection.

rows.verbatim:
Manage and store POL products in accordance with EPA 40 CFR
112, and other federal, state, regional, and local laws and regulations.
rows.normalized: Contractor must manage and store POL products per 40 CFR 112 and applicable laws.

rows.verbatim:
Use secondary containments, dikes, curbs, and other barriers, to prevent
POL products from spilling and entering the ground, storm or sewer drains,
stormwater ditches or canals, or navigable waters of the United States.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use secondary containment measures to prevent POL spills from entering drains/waters.

rows.verbatim:
Describe in the EPP (see paragraph ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION PLAN) how POL
tanks and containers must be stored, managed, and inspected and what
protections must be provided.
rows.normalized: Contractor must describe in the EPP how POL tanks/containers will be stored, managed, inspected, and protected.

rows.verbatim:
Storage of fuel on the project site must be
in accordance with EPA, state, and local laws and regulations and
paragraph OIL STORAGE INCLUDING FUEL TANKS.
rows.normalized: Fuel storage on the project site must comply with EPA, state, local laws and the Oil Storage paragraph.

rows.verbatim: Manage used oil generated on site in accordance with 40 CFR 279.
rows.normalized: Contractor must manage used oil generated on site per 40 CFR 279.

rows.verbatim:
Determine if any used oil generated while onsite exhibits a characteristic
of hazardous waste.
rows.normalized: Contractor must determine if used oil generated onsite exhibits hazardous waste characteristics.

rows.verbatim:
Used oil containing 1,000 parts per million of
solvents is considered a hazardous waste and disposed of at the
Contractor's expense.
rows.normalized: Used oil with 1,000 ppm solvents is hazardous waste and must be disposed of at Contractor's expense.

rows.verbatim:
Dispose in accordance with paragraph
HAZARDOUS WASTE DISPOSAL.
rows.normalized: Contractor must dispose of such waste per the Hazardous Waste Disposal paragraph.

rows.verbatim:
Provide secondary containment and overfill protection for oil storage
tanks.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide secondary containment and overfill protection for oil storage tanks.

rows.verbatim:
A berm used to provide secondary containment
must be of sufficient size and strength to contain the contents of the
tanks plus 5 inches freeboard for precipitation.
rows.normalized: Berms for secondary containment must hold tank contents plus 5 inches freeboard for precipitation.

rows.verbatim:
Construct the berm to be impervious to oil for 72 hours that no discharge will permeate, drain, infiltrate, or
otherwise escape before cleanup occurs.
rows.normalized: Contractor must construct berms impervious to oil for 72 hours to prevent discharge before cleanup.

rows.verbatim:
Use drip pans during oil transfer
operations; adequate absorbent material must be onsite to clean up any
spills and prevent releases to the environment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use drip pans during oil transfer and have adequate absorbent material onsite.

rows.verbatim:
Cover tanks and drip pans
during inclement weather.
rows.normalized: Contractor must cover tanks and drip pans during inclement weather.

rows.verbatim:
If tanks and containers
with an aggregate aboveground capacity greater than 1320 gallons will be
used onsite (only containers with a capacity of 55 gallons or greater are
counted), provide and implement a SPCC plan meeting the requirements of
40 CFR 112.
rows.normalized: If aboveground tank/container capacity onsite exceeds 1320 gallons, contractor must provide and implement an SPCC plan meeting 40 CFR 112.

rows.verbatim:
Do not
bring underground storage tanks for Contractor use during a project.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not bring underground storage tanks for its use during the project.

rows.verbatim: Include the SPCC plan in the EPP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must include the SPCC plan in the EPP.

rows.verbatim:
Monitor and remove any rainwater that accumulates in open containment
dikes or berms.
rows.normalized: Contractor must monitor and remove rainwater accumulated in open containment dikes or berms.

rows.verbatim:
Inspect the accumulated rainwater prior to draining from
a containment dike to the environment, to determine there is no oil sheen
present.
rows.normalized: Contractor must inspect accumulated rainwater for oil sheen before draining from containment dikes.

rows.verbatim:
If petroleum-contaminated soil, or suspected hazardous waste is found
during dredging operation that was not identified in the Contract
documents, immediately notify the Government.
rows.normalized: If petroleum-contaminated soil or suspected hazardous waste not identified in contract documents is found, contractor must immediately notify the Government.

rows.verbatim: Do not disturb this material until authorized by the Government.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not disturb the discovered material until authorized by the Government.

rows.verbatim:
Make the maximum use of low-noise emission products, as certified by the
EPA.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make maximum use of EPA-certified low-noise emission products.

rows.verbatim: Blasting or use of explosives are not permitted.
rows.normalized: Blasting or use of explosives is prohibited.

rows.verbatim:
Keep construction activities under surveillance and control to minimize
environment damage by noise.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep construction activities under surveillance and control to minimize noise damage.

rows.verbatim: Comply with the provisions of the State of California rules.
rows.normalized: Contractor must comply with State of California noise rules.

rows.verbatim: Clean up in accordance with Contract Clause: "Cleaning Up".
rows.normalized: Contractor must clean up per the Contract Clause "Cleaning Up".

rows.verbatim:
Unless otherwise instructed in writing by the Government,
remove traces of construction, and other vestiges prior to final
acceptance of the work.
rows.normalized: Unless the Government instructs otherwise in writing, contractor must remove traces of construction and other vestiges before final acceptance.

rows.verbatim:
Government approval is required for submittals with a "G"
designation; submittals not having a "G" designation are for information
only.
rows.normalized: Submittals with a G designation require Government approval; others are for information only.

rows.verbatim:
Submit the following in accordance with Section 01 33 00 SUBMITTAL
PROCEDURES:
SD-07 Certificates
Herring Observer Resumes; G
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit Herring Observer Resumes (SD-07, G) per Section 01 33 00.

rows.verbatim:
Herring spawning observers are required day and night (24 hrs/day) for all
dredging operations that occur after November 30 and before March 16 in
any year for reaches 0, 1 and 2.
rows.normalized: Herring spawning observers are required 24 hrs/day for dredging in reaches 0,1,2 between Nov 30 and Mar 16.

rows.verbatim:
Contractor shall provide trained observers in accordance with instructions included in the HERRING SPAWNING
OBSERVERS paragraph below.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide trained herring spawning observers per the referenced paragraph.

rows.verbatim:
Herring Observer Resumes
shall be submitted to the Government for review and approval prior to any
in-water work after November 30 and before March 16.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit herring observer resumes to the Government for approval before in-water work in the restricted period.

rows.verbatim:
Any material dredged after November 30 in
any year shall be placed at an upland beneficial reuse site benefitting
aquatic species, as directed by the Government.
rows.normalized: Material dredged after November 30 shall be placed at an upland beneficial reuse site as directed.

rows.verbatim:
The contractor shall provide to the Government herring observer resumes
which must include in the beginning of the qualifications whether or not
the observer is a CDFW approved biologist and if so list the date of the
training.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide herring observer resumes that must state CDFW-approved biologist status and training date.

rows.verbatim:
Government approval of the resumes is
required prior to any in-water work between November 30 and before March
16.
rows.normalized: Government approval of resumes is required before in-water work in the restricted period, creating a contractor dependency.

rows.verbatim:
The Contractor is
responsible for acquiring the services of CDFW-approved biologist(s) to
observe and record data documenting herring spawning activities during all
dredging operations after 30 November.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for acquiring CDFW-approved biologists to observe/record herring spawning data after Nov 30.

rows.verbatim:
The biologist(s)must have a Bachelor of
Science degree in Biology and experience with fish in the San Francisco
bay.
rows.normalized: Biologists must have a B.S. in Biology and experience with San Francisco Bay fish.

rows.verbatim:
The contractor shall provide at least one approved biologist per dredge
plant.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide at least one approved biologist per dredge plant.

rows.verbatim:
The observing activities shall be documented in accordance
with CDFW guidance shown in Attachment 1 Daily Biological Observation Log
attached at the end of the specification package.
rows.normalized: Observing activities shall be documented per CDFW guidance in Attachment 1.

rows.verbatim:
The daily biological observation logs shall be submitted to CDFW,
Government and the COR on a daily basis.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit daily biological observation logs to CDFW, Government, and COR daily.

rows.verbatim:
The observer(s) will immediately notify the Contractor, COR,
Government, and CDFW when spawning activity is observed within 500-meters
of dredging activities, and the Contractor shall immediately move to an
area outside of the 500-meter buffer to continue dredging and may not
resume dredging in the area where spawning was observed until given
permission by the Contracting Officer or designated representative.
rows.normalized: When spawning activity is observed within 500m, contractor shall immediately move outside the buffer and may not resume dredging there until permitted by the Contracting Officer.

rows.verbatim:
Government approval is required for submittals with a "G" designation:
submittals not having a "G" designation are for information only.
rows.normalized: Submittals with a G designation require Government approval; others are for information only.

rows.verbatim:
Submit the following in accordance with Section SUBMITTAL PROCEDURES 01 33 00:
SD-01 Preconstruction Submittals
Work Plan; G
Coast Guard Notification
Dredge Data Logging System (DDLS); G
SD-10 Operation and Maintenance Data
Dredge Material Disposal Site Log (DMDSL)
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit listed preconstruction and O&M submittals (Work Plan, Coast Guard Notification, DDLS, DMDSL) per Section 01 33 00.

rows.verbatim:
Submit a DMDSL on a weekly basis by noon Monday that enumerates work
accomplished during the preceding week.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit the DMDSL weekly by noon Monday covering the prior week's work.

rows.verbatim:
The DMDSL log to be submitted
shall include the reach from where the material came from.
rows.normalized: The submitted DMDSL log shall include the reach the material came from.

rows.verbatim:
Every Monday, the Contractor shall e-mail the prior week's DMDSL data to
the government.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall e-mail the prior week's DMDSL data to the Government every Monday.

rows.verbatim:
Maintain a DMDSL using the "Dredge Material Disposal Site Log" form
attached at the end of the Specification package.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain a DMDSL using the attached form.

rows.verbatim:
DMDSL shall be included
as an attachment to QC Daily Reports.
rows.normalized: DMDSL shall be included as an attachment to QC Daily Reports.

rows.verbatim:
Methods used for the dredge positioning shall also be used to display and
record the disposal vessel's location at 1-minute time intervals
throughout the loading, transport and disposal cycle of each disposal
vessel.
rows.normalized: Dredge positioning methods shall also record disposal vessel location at 1-minute intervals throughout the disposal cycle.

rows.verbatim:
The Dredge Data Logging System (DDLS) data shall be received
onboard the actual disposal vessel.
rows.normalized: DDLS data shall be received onboard the actual disposal vessel.

rows.verbatim:
Position data shall be annotated for the time actual dumping is in
progress.
rows.normalized: Position data shall be annotated for the time actual dumping occurs.

rows.verbatim:
A copy record of the DDLS position
data, correlated with time and annotated with date, shall be submitted to
the Contracting Officer or delegated representative as part of the daily
Quality Control Report.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit a dated/correlated copy of DDLS position data with the daily QC Report.

rows.verbatim:
Dredge inspectors shall be provided with hand-held GPS equipment to verify dredge disposal in
SF-DODS.
rows.normalized: Dredge inspectors shall be provided hand-held GPS equipment to verify dredge disposal in SF-DODS.

rows.verbatim:
Submit electronic copies of the DDLS positional data for all dredge
equipment and all disposal/fill vessels utilized; and dredged quantity,
sediment type and GPS positional data on the dredge and disposal or fill
locations for all scows and barges by email to the government.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit electronic DDLS positional and dredge quantity/sediment data by email to the Government.

rows.verbatim: This electronic data shall be included in the daily CQC Report submitted in RMS.
rows.normalized: The electronic DDLS data shall be included in the daily CQC Report submitted in RMS.

rows.verbatim:
The work plan should be submitted within 15 days after Notice to Proceed
or prior to the date of the Preconstruction Conference.
rows.normalized: Contractor should submit the work plan within 15 days after Notice to Proceed or before the Preconstruction Conference.

rows.verbatim:
Revise the work plan throughout the project to include any changes in site
conditions or contract modifications that change the project scope of work.
rows.normalized: Contractor must revise the work plan to reflect site condition changes or scope-changing contract modifications.

rows.verbatim: Dredging in excess of the allowable 2-foot overdepth is prohibited.
rows.normalized: Dredging beyond the allowable 2-foot overdepth is prohibited.

rows.verbatim: Dredging on the side slope is prohibited.
rows.normalized: Dredging on the side slope is prohibited.

rows.verbatim: All BD and AD surveys are performed in accordance with Section HYDROGRAPHIC SURVEY 01 32 23.
rows.normalized: BD and AD surveys must be performed per Section 01 32 23.

rows.verbatim: All work shall be performed in accordance with the conditions and requirements included in the state and federal permits applicable to this project.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall perform all work per applicable state and federal permit conditions/requirements.

rows.verbatim: Base bids on total cubic yards of dredging.
rows.normalized: Contractor must base bids on total cubic yards of dredging.

rows.verbatim: Include a bid unit price per cubic yard of dredging based on the quantity as specified or indicated.
rows.normalized: Contractor must include a bid unit price per cubic yard of dredging based on specified/indicated quantity.

rows.verbatim: However, the Contractor is responsible for other conditions encountered which are not unusual when compared to conditions recognized in the dredging business as usual in dredging activities such as those required under this contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for other, not-unusual conditions encountered during dredging.

rows.verbatim: Inspect the work, keep records of work performed, and ensure that gages, targets, ranges, and other markers are in place and usable for the intended purpose.
rows.normalized: Contractor must inspect the work, keep records, and ensure gages/markers are in place and usable.

rows.verbatim: Furnish, at the request of the Contracting Officer or delegated representative, boats, boatmen, laborers, and materials necessary for inspecting, supervising, and surveying the work.
rows.normalized: If requested by the CO or delegate, Contractor must furnish boats, boatmen, laborers, and materials for inspection/supervision/survey.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall provide, upon request of the Government QA Representative (GQAR), suitable transportation from all points on shore designated by the GQAR to and from the various pieces of plant, and to and from the dredging and disposal areas.
rows.normalized: Upon GQAR request, Contractor shall provide transportation between shore points, plant, and dredging/disposal areas.

rows.verbatim: Transportation will be made available during all shift changes, when requested by GQAR.
rows.normalized: Contractor must make transportation available during shift changes when GQAR requests it.

rows.verbatim: Contractor should anticipate at least two round trips per 24-hour period.
rows.normalized: Contractor should plan for at least two round trips per 24-hour period.

rows.verbatim: Contractor shall provide GQAR access to a desk, or other suitable workspace including electrical outlet, while on-board the dredge plant.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall provide GQAR desk/workspace with electrical outlet on the dredge plant.

rows.verbatim: Minimize interference of channels and passages.
rows.normalized: Contractor must minimize interference with channels and passages.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor is responsible for shifting or moving of dredges or the interruption of dredging operations to accommodate the movement of vessels and floating equipment, if necessary.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for shifting/moving dredges or interrupting operations to accommodate vessel movement.

rows.verbatim: Adhere to Coast Guard Regulations for passing vessels.
rows.normalized: Contractor must adhere to Coast Guard regulations for passing vessels.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor will be required to conduct the work in such a manner as to obstruct navigation as little as possible, and in the event the Contractor's plant so obstructs the channel as to make difficult or endanger the passage of any vessels, the plant shall be promptly moved on the approach of any vessel to such an extent as may be necessary to afford a practicable passage.
rows.normalized: Contractor must minimize navigation obstruction and, if its plant obstructs the channel, shall promptly move the plant to allow vessel passage.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor shall submit copies of written Coast Guard notifications prior to conducting dredging activities.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall submit copies of written Coast Guard notifications before dredging.

rows.verbatim: Utilize the Work Plan to forecast the activities in the channels and notify the United States Coast Guard Marine Safety Office in writing with a copy to the Contracting Office Representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use the Work Plan to forecast channel activities and notify USCG Marine Safety Office in writing, copying the COR.

rows.verbatim: All Coast Guard notifications shall be provided in accordance with Section GOVERNMENT SAFETY REQUIREMENTS (DREDGING) 01 35 26 U.S. Coast Guard Notification and Marine Transportation Safety.
rows.normalized: All Coast Guard notifications shall follow Section 01 35 26 requirements.

rows.verbatim: All dredge plants must be equipped with an Automatic Identification System (AIS) transponder that is compatible with Coast Guard specifications identified in Section GOVERNMENT SAFETY REQUIREMENTS (DREDGING) 01 35 26 Vessel Traffic Services (VTS) Reporting Requirements.
rows.normalized: All dredge plants must have an AIS transponder compatible with Coast Guard VTS specifications in Section 01 35 26.

rows.verbatim: Each night, between sunset and sunrise and during periods of restricted visibility, provide lights for floating plants, pipelines, ranges, and markers.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide lights for floating plants, pipelines, ranges, and markers at night/restricted visibility.

rows.verbatim: Also, provide lights for buoys that could endanger or obstruct navigation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide lights for buoys that could endanger/obstruct navigation.

rows.verbatim: When night work is in progress, maintain lights from sunset to sunrise for the observation of dredging operations.
rows.normalized: When night work occurs, Contractor must maintain lights from sunset to sunrise for observation.

rows.verbatim: Lighting shall conform to United States Coast Guard requirements for visibility and color.
rows.normalized: Lighting shall conform to USCG visibility/color requirements.

rows.verbatim: Furnish, set, and maintain DGPS-based electronic positioning systems capable of displaying the real-time dredge plant position and the project limits and/or ranges, buoys, and markers needed to define the work and to facilitate inspection.
rows.normalized: Contractor must furnish, set, and maintain DGPS positioning systems showing real-time plant position and project limits.

rows.verbatim: Suspend dredging when the positioning system cannot be seen or followed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must suspend dredging when the positioning system cannot be seen/followed.

rows.verbatim: Maintain the plant, scows, coamings, barges, pipelines, and associated equipment to meet the requirements of the work.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain plant/equipment to meet work requirements.

rows.verbatim: Promptly repair leaks or breaks along pipelines.
rows.normalized: Contractor must promptly repair pipeline leaks/breaks.

rows.verbatim: Remove dredged material placed due to leaks and breaks.
rows.normalized: Contractor must remove dredged material placed due to leaks/breaks.

rows.verbatim: Provide for safe transportation and disposal of dredged materials.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide safe transportation and disposal of dredged materials.

rows.verbatim: Transport and dispose of dredged material per the requirements in section 00 10 00 Pricing Schedule, unless otherwise directed by the Contracting Officer or delegated representative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must transport/dispose dredged material per Section 00 10 00, unless otherwise directed by CO/delegate.

rows.verbatim: The deposit of dredged materials in unauthorized places is forbidden.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not deposit dredged materials in unauthorized places.

rows.verbatim: Comply with rules and regulations of local port and harbor governing authorities.
rows.normalized: Contractor must comply with local port/harbor rules and regulations.

rows.verbatim: Deposit dredged material per the requirements of section 00 10 00 Pricing Schedule by scow or barge, and using an appropriate method to unload scow/barge to place material within the sites specified in section 00 10 00 Pricing Schedule.
rows.normalized: Contractor must deposit dredged material by scow/barge per Section 00 10 00, placing it within specified sites.

rows.verbatim: In depositing excavated material for fill, uniformly grade and allow for shrinkage.
rows.normalized: Contractor must uniformly grade fill material and allow for shrinkage.

rows.verbatim: Provide and maintain necessary bulkheads, dikes, ditches, weirs, spillways, and other construction necessary to confine and retain the fill in the dredge fill area.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide/maintain structures to confine and retain fill in the dredge fill area.

rows.verbatim: Overflow/decant, spillage and leakage is prohibited during transportation to the disposal site.
rows.normalized: Overflow/decant, spillage, and leakage during transport to disposal site is prohibited.

rows.verbatim: Decanting and overflow at the dredging site shall be in the accordance with the environmental permits and documents.
rows.normalized: Decanting/overflow at the dredging site shall follow environmental permits and documents.

rows.verbatim: Barring, dragging and all other methods of bed leveling are prohibited.
rows.normalized: Barring, dragging, and other bed-leveling methods are prohibited.

rows.verbatim: Before transport to SF-DODS all dredged material must be placed into scows through a steel mesh or chain "grizzly" with openings of no more than 12 inches by 12 inches.
rows.normalized: Before transport to SF-DODS, dredged material must pass through a grizzly with openings no larger than 12x12 inches.

rows.verbatim: Furnish and maintain, if applicable, navigation warning signs along the pipeline.
rows.normalized: If applicable, Contractor must furnish and maintain navigation warning signs along the pipeline.

rows.verbatim: Provide a system of communication between the dredge crew and the crew at the disposal area.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a communication system between dredge crew and disposal-area crew.

rows.verbatim: The execution of work shall ensure the stability of piers, bulkheads, and other structures lying on or adjacent to the site of the work, insofar as structures may be jeopardized by dredging operations.
rows.normalized: Contractor's execution of work shall ensure stability of piers/bulkheads/structures jeopardized by dredging.

rows.verbatim: Repair damage resulting from dredging operations, insofar as such damage may be caused by variation in locations or depth of dredging, or both, from that indicated or permitted under the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must repair damage caused by dredging variations from indicated/permitted locations or depths.

rows.verbatim: Upon completion of the work, promptly remove plant, including ranges, buoys, piles, and other markers or obstructions.
rows.normalized: Upon completion, Contractor must promptly remove plant, ranges, buoys, piles, and other markers/obstructions.

rows.verbatim: Acceptance of soundings shall be in accordance with Section HYDROGRAPHIC SURVEY 01 32 23
rows.normalized: Soundings acceptance shall follow Section 01 32 23 requirements.

rows.verbatim: Any shoals, lumps, or other lack of required contract depth disclosed by the After-Dredge survey shall be removed by dredging the channel bottom at the contract rate for dredging.
rows.normalized: Contractor shall remove shoals/lumps or depth deficiencies disclosed by the After-Dredge survey at the contract dredging rate.

rows.verbatim: No shoals or lumps above contract depth, as evidenced by multi-beam sounding will be accepted.
rows.normalized: Shoals/lumps above contract depth, as shown by multi-beam sounding, will not be accepted (pass/fail criterion).

rows.verbatim: There will be no separate payment for installation, operation, and maintenance of the DQM-certified system in connection with this contract and are considered covered under the contract unit price for dredging in the bid schedule.
rows.normalized: No separate payment applies for DQM system installation/operation/maintenance; costs are covered under the unit price for dredging.

rows.verbatim: The work under this contract requires use of the US Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Dredging Quality Management (DQM) Program to monitor all dredge plants at all times throughout the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use the USACE DQM Program to monitor all dredge plants at all times.

rows.verbatim: DQM monitoring is required on all equipment (to be called plants) used on this contract to excavate, transport, or place dredged material.
rows.normalized: DQM monitoring is required on all equipment used to excavate, transport, or place dredged material.

rows.verbatim: Current certification from the DQM Center for all dredge plants to be used under this contract is required.
rows.normalized: Current DQM Center certification is required for all dredge plants used under the contract.

rows.verbatim: DQM certification is contingent upon the Contractor's system's ability to meet the performance requirements as outlined in SYSTEM TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS and OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE, REPORTING AND QA, including all subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: DQM certification depends on the Contractor's system meeting the System Technical Requirements and Operational Performance/Reporting/QA requirements.

rows.verbatim: If performance requirements are not met and maintained, DQM certification may be revoked.
rows.normalized: If performance requirements are not met/maintained, DQM certification may be revoked.

rows.verbatim:
DQM Certification for dredge plants is based on the following:
• The requirements outlined in SYSTEM TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS,
including all subparagraphs.
• Review of the Dredge Plant Instrumentation Plan (DPIP) as described in
DREDGE PLANT INSTRUMENTATION PLAN (DPIP).
• Onsite QA checks as outlined on the DQM website (https://dqm.usace.army.mil)
and described in ONSITE QUALITY ASSURANCE (QA) CHECK.
• Data transmission and quality maintained throughout the duration of the contract
as described in OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE, REPORTING AND QA,
including all subparagraphs.
• Timely communication and corrective action in response to QA notifications as
required by QUALITY ASSURANCE COMMENTS.
• Accurate and timely entry of data as described in STATE DATA.
rows.normalized: DQM certification is based on six listed elements: system technical requirements, DPIP review, onsite QA checks, data transmission/quality maintenance, timely QA response, and accurate/timely data entry.

rows.verbatim: Contact the DQM Center at dqm-support@usace.army.mil at least three weeks prior to certification expiration, to schedule and coordinate QA checks for certification renewal.
rows.normalized: Contractor must contact the DQM Center at least three weeks before certification expiration to schedule recertification QA checks.

rows.verbatim: At least one week prior to the target date, the DQM Center must be contacted to verbally coordinate a specific date and location.
rows.normalized: Contractor must contact the DQM Center at least one week before the target date to verbally coordinate a specific date/location.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor must then follow up this conversation with a written email confirmation.
rows.normalized: Contractor must follow up the verbal coordination with a written email confirmation.

rows.verbatim: Recertification is required for changes in sensor type or location as well as any yard work that produces modification to reported values.
rows.normalized: Recertification is required for sensor type/location changes or yard work modifying reported values.

rows.verbatim: A plant does not have to be transmitting data between jobs; however, to retain its DQM certification, the sensors or hardware must not be disconnected or removed from the plant.
rows.normalized: To retain DQM certification, sensors/hardware must not be disconnected or removed between jobs.

rows.verbatim: If the system is powered down, calibration coefficients must be retained.
rows.normalized: If the system is powered down, calibration coefficients must be retained.

rows.verbatim: Contractor/subcontractor personnel who are familiar with the instrumentation and can recalibrate the sensors must be on site during the QA process.
rows.normalized: Contractor/subcontractor personnel familiar with instrumentation and able to recalibrate sensors must be on site during QA checks.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor will coordinate pickup times and locations and provide transportation to and from any vessel with a DQM system to team personnel in a timely manner.
rows.normalized: Contractor will coordinate pickup times/locations and provide timely transportation to/from DQM-equipped vessels for team personnel.

rows.verbatim: If additional safety equipment is needed, such as eye protection, safety harnesses, work gloves, or personal location beacons— the Contractor must provide these items to the DQM QA team while on site.
rows.normalized: If additional safety equipment is needed, Contractor must provide it to the DQM QA team on site.

rows.verbatim: It is the Contractor's obligation to inform the DQM QA team if the location designated for the QA checks has any site-specific safety concerns prior to their arrival on site.
rows.normalized: Contractor must inform the DQM QA team of any site-specific safety concerns before their arrival.

rows.verbatim: A digital copy of the DPIP must be on file with the DQM Center.
rows.normalized: A digital DPIP copy must be on file with the DQM Center.

rows.verbatim: While working on site, the Contractor will maintain on the plant a copy of the DPIP, which is always easily accessible to Government personnel.
rows.normalized: While working on site, Contractor will maintain an accessible DPIP copy on the plant.

rows.verbatim: This document must accurately describe the sensors used, the configuration of the system, how sensor data will be collected, how quality control on the data will be performed, and how the sensors/data-reporting equipment will be calibrated and repaired if it fails.
rows.normalized: The DPIP must accurately describe sensors, system configuration, data collection, QC, and calibration/repair procedures.

rows.verbatim: A description of the computed plant-specific data and how the sensor data will be transmitted to the DQM database must also be included.
rows.normalized: The DPIP must also include a description of computed plant-specific data and data transmission to the DQM database.

rows.verbatim: Prior to the start of work any addendum or modifications made to the plan after its original submission must be submitted to the DQM Center.
rows.normalized: Before start of work, any DPIP addenda/modifications must be submitted to the DQM Center.

rows.verbatim: Any changes to the computation methods must be approved by the DQM Center prior to their implementation.
rows.normalized: Changes to computation methods must be approved by the DQM Center before implementation.

rows.verbatim: Keep a log of sensor repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations in the DPIP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must keep a log of sensor repairs/replacements/installations/modifications/calibrations in the DPIP.

rows.verbatim: The log must contain a three-year history of sensor maintenance, including the time of the sensor failures (and subsequent repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations), the time and results of sensor calibrations, the time of sensor replacements, and the time that backup sensor systems were initiated to provide the required data.
rows.normalized: The sensor log must contain a three-year maintenance history including failure times, repairs, calibration results, replacements, and backup-system initiation times.

rows.verbatim: It must also contain the name of the person responsible for the sensor work.
rows.normalized: The log must also contain the name of the person responsible for the sensor work.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor must provide, operate, and maintain all hardware and software to meet these specifications for the respective plant types on the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide, operate, and maintain all hardware and software to meet the specified data collection requirements for each plant type.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor is responsible for the repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations of the sensors and any other equipment needed to collect and transmit the required data.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, and calibrations of sensors and other equipment needed to collect and transmit required data.

rows.verbatim: Sensors installed must be capable of collecting and reporting parameters at the specified interval, accuracy, precision, and resolution as described in DATA PARAMETERS BY PLANT TYPE, including all subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: Installed sensors must be capable of collecting and reporting parameters at the specified interval, accuracy, precision, and resolution.

rows.verbatim: Data will be logged and archived locally onboard the plant as a backup to transmitted data as described in DATA BACKUP REQUIREMENTS.
rows.normalized: The system (contractor-provided) will log and archive data locally onboard the plant as a backup to transmitted data.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor must provide an easily accessible visual display onboard the plant that displays in real time the raw parameters collected by the system in the same units as are used for data submitted to DQM.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide an easily accessible onboard visual display showing real-time raw parameters in the same units as data submitted to DQM.

rows.verbatim: In the event a reported parameter is calculated based on multiple sensors, the sensor values as used in the equation must be visible in addition to the required parameter.
rows.normalized: If a reported parameter is calculated from multiple sensors, the underlying sensor values used in the equation must also be visible.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor is responsible for acquiring, installing, and maintaining all necessary hardware and software to ensure reliable internet connectivity for data transmission to the DQM web service.
rows.normalized: Contractor is responsible for acquiring, installing, and maintaining hardware/software to ensure reliable internet connectivity for data transmission to DQM.

rows.verbatim: The internet connection must support real-time data transmission and provide sufficient bandwidth to clear any queued data when connectivity is restored after an outage.
rows.normalized: The internet connection must support real-time transmission and sufficient bandwidth to clear queued data after an outage.

rows.verbatim: Data collected must be transmitted to the DQM web service in real-time, in accordance with the standards outlined in DATA PARAMETERS BY PLANT TYPE and all related subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: Collected data must be transmitted to the DQM web service in real-time per specified standards.

rows.verbatim: Scow data transmission must be fully automated end-to-end.
rows.normalized: Scow data transmission must be fully automated end-to-end.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor may transmit directly from the scow or via a shore-based relay. When a relay is used: (a) the scow must transmit to the relay no less frequently than every 4 hours, and (b) the relay must forward to the DQM web service immediately and automatically upon receipt.
rows.normalized: Contractor may transmit directly or via relay; if a relay is used, the scow must transmit to it at least every 4 hours and the relay must forward data to DQM immediately and automatically upon receipt.

rows.verbatim: If internet connectivity is lost, the web service is unavailable, or data cannot be transmitted for any reason, unsent data should be queued and transmitted immediately upon restoration of connectivity.
rows.normalized: If connectivity or the web service is unavailable, unsent data should be queued and transmitted immediately upon restoration.

rows.verbatim: Transmission should begin with the oldest data in the queue and continue until real-time transmission resumes.
rows.normalized: Queued transmission should begin with oldest data and continue until real-time transmission resumes.

rows.verbatim: Contact dqm-support@usace.army.mil for transmission details, such as the DQM web service URL, headers, authorization credentials, and communication protocol information.
rows.normalized: Contractor should contact DQM support for transmission details (URL, headers, credentials, protocol info).

rows.verbatim: Collected sensor data will be compiled into correctly formatted data strings for transmission to DQM.
rows.normalized: Collected sensor data must be compiled into correctly formatted data strings for transmission to DQM.

rows.verbatim:
Data string format varies by plant type:
Hopper: XML
Scow: XML
Pipeline: JSON
Mechanical: JSON
rows.normalized: Data string format specification table by plant type (Hopper/Scow=XML, Pipeline/Mechanical=JSON), page 282, 4 items.

rows.verbatim: All data strings contain a minimum of two data parameters, a plant identifier assigned by the DQM Center and a Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) stamp based on a 24-hour format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
rows.normalized: All data strings must contain at minimum two parameters: a DQM-assigned plant identifier and a UTC timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).

rows.verbatim: Other data parameters vary by plant type or profile and will be enclosed within the appropriate XML or JSON tag.
rows.normalized: Other data parameters, which vary by plant type, must be enclosed within the appropriate XML or JSON tag.

rows.verbatim: If a parameter is not applicable or otherwise missing, it will be omitted from the data string.
rows.normalized: If a parameter is not applicable or missing, it will be omitted from the data string.

rows.verbatim: Data must be collected and transmitted at set intervals (which vary by plant type and activity state) as outlined in the table below.
rows.normalized: Contractor must collect and transmit data at set intervals per plant type/activity state per the table below.

rows.verbatim: Raw sensor samples reported in a data string must be acquired no more than 1 second before the timestamp of that string.
rows.normalized: Raw sensor samples must be acquired no more than 1 second before the string's timestamp.

rows.verbatim: Averaged or computed parameters must be derived from samples acquired within the reporting interval as outlined in the table below.
rows.normalized: Averaged/computed parameters must be derived from samples acquired within the reporting interval per the table below.

rows.verbatim: Any sensor data averaging or calculations performed externally to the sensors must be documented in the DPIP.
rows.normalized: If sensor data averaging/calculations are performed externally to sensors, they must be documented in the DPIP.

rows.verbatim:
Plant Type Event Type Reporting Interval
Hopper ALL 6-12 seconds
Pipeline ALL 6-12 seconds
Mechanical Time Interval 1 minute
Mechanical Dig/Dump A data point must be recorded within 1 second of a
bucket “dig” or “dump” event occurring.
Scow Loading/Sailing/ 1 minute
Offloading/Idle SOLICITATION
Scow Open Water A data point must be recorded within 1 second of the
Placement hull status going from closed to open and again within
1 second of the hull status going from open to closed.
Between these events, report the data at an equal
interval from 6 to 12 seconds. This interval must
always remain consistent for the dredge plant.
rows.normalized: Data frequency/reporting interval table by plant type and event type, page 282, listing required reporting intervals (e.g., Hopper/Pipeline 6-12 sec, Mechanical 1 min/dig-dump within 1 sec, Scow 1 min/open-water event timing); table, about 6 entries.

rows.verbatim: An archive of all data sent to the DQM Center in the format that it was originally collected and transmitted must be maintained.
rows.normalized: Contractor must maintain an archive of all data sent to the DQM Center in the format it was originally collected and transmitted.

rows.verbatim: This archive will be preserved by the Contractor for a minimum of one year past the end of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor will preserve the archive for a minimum of one year past the end of the contract.

rows.verbatim: At the completion of dredging activities all data gaps must be filled or addressed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must fill or address all data gaps at the completion of dredging activities.

rows.verbatim: When data backup includes unresolved data gaps the Contractor must follow the guidance described in DATA GAPS.
rows.normalized: If data backup includes unresolved data gaps, Contractor must follow the guidance described in DATA GAPS.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor’s data transmission system must be operational at the start of dredging operations and certified prior to moving dredge material on the contract (see paragraph CERTIFICATION).
rows.normalized: Contractor's data transmission system must be operational at the start of dredging operations and certified before moving dredge material.

rows.verbatim: The plant must maintain DQM certification and remain compliant throughout the duration of the contract.
rows.normalized: Contractor's plant must maintain DQM certification and remain compliant throughout the contract duration.

rows.verbatim: In addition to real-time work event messages, submissions of “state data” are also required for hoppers, pipeline, and mechanical plant types.
rows.normalized: Contractor is required to submit state data for hopper, pipeline, and mechanical plant types.

rows.verbatim: State data must be submitted daily, reporting on all activities for the prior day.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit state data daily, reporting on all activities for the prior day.

rows.verbatim: Prior to commencement of project startup and at the completion of work DQM must be notified by emailing dqm-support@usace.army.mil.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify DQM by email prior to project startup and at completion of work.

rows.verbatim: The notification must include the plants working on the project, estimated project duration, and project personnel who need access to DQM.
rows.normalized: Contractor's notification to DQM must include the plants working on the project, estimated project duration, and personnel needing DQM access.

rows.verbatim: Data will be logged locally onboard the plant as a backup of transmitted data.
rows.normalized: System must log data locally onboard the plant as backup of transmitted data.

rows.verbatim: A work event message includes all required sensor data, computed parameters, and a timestamp corresponding to the event or interval.
rows.normalized: A work event message must include all required sensor data, computed parameters, and a timestamp for the event/interval.

rows.verbatim: Each work event message is formatted and transmitted in accordance with the requirements outlined in DATA FORMAT and DATA TRANSMISSION.
rows.normalized: Each work event message must be formatted and transmitted per DATA FORMAT and DATA TRANSMISSION requirements.

rows.verbatim: State data entries are submitted daily through the DQM Contractor Management Site from the first day of dredging activity on the contract through the final day.
rows.normalized: Contractor must submit state data entries daily via the DQM Contractor Management Site from first through last day of dredging activity.

rows.verbatim: In the event of a system outage that results in a data gap which cannot be filled with backup data, provide a clear explanation documenting the cause and duration of the gap.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide a clear explanation of cause and duration when a system outage causes a data gap that cannot be filled with backup data.

rows.verbatim: Record this explanation using the DQM Contractor Management Site within 48 hours.
rows.normalized: Contractor must record the data-gap explanation in the DQM Contractor Management Site within 48 hours.

rows.verbatim: The Contractor will submit a response within 48 hours of receiving any QA notification identifying immediate mitigations and an estimated restoration schedule.
rows.normalized: Contractor will submit a response within 48 hours of receiving any QA notification, identifying immediate mitigations and an estimated restoration schedule.

rows.verbatim: All notifications, actions, and supporting records will be entered in DQM Contractor Management Site.
rows.normalized: Contractor will enter all notifications, actions, and supporting records in the DQM Contractor Management Site.

rows.verbatim: If hardware problems occur, or if a part of the system is physically damaged, the Contractor is responsible for repairs.
rows.normalized: If hardware problems occur or a system part is physically damaged, the Contractor is responsible for repairs.

rows.verbatim: Sensor failures must be documented on the DQM Contractor Management Site.
rows.normalized: Contractor must document sensor failures on the DQM Contractor Management Site.

rows.verbatim: Corrective action (repair, replacement, or recalibration) must be completed within 48 hours of discovery.
rows.normalized: Contractor must complete corrective action (repair, replacement, or recalibration) within 48 hours of discovery.

rows.verbatim: If 48-hour completion is not feasible, the Contractor must notify the DQM Center before the 48-hour deadline with cause and estimated completion date.
rows.normalized: If 48-hour completion is not feasible, the Contractor must notify the DQM Center before the 48-hour deadline with cause and estimated completion date.

rows.verbatim: Upon completion of repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, or calibrations, notify the DQM Center.
rows.normalized: Contractor must notify the DQM Center upon completion of repairs, replacements, installations, modifications, or calibrations.

rows.verbatim:
3.4.1 LIST OF ITEMS TO BE PROVIDED BY THE CONTRACTOR
DPIP Paragraph DREDGE PLANT
INSTRUMENTATION PLAN (DPIP) and DQM
Center website https://dqm.usace.army.mil. SOLICITATION
INSTRUMENTATION SYSTEM Paragraph SYSTEM TECHNICAL
AND DATA REQUIREMENTS, including all subparagraphs.
EVENT DOCUMENTATION Paragraph OPERATIONAL PERFORMANCE,
REPORTING AND QA, including all
subparagraphs.
rows.normalized: Table of items the Contractor must provide (DPIP, Instrumentation System, Event Documentation references), SOW 3.4.1, page 284, 3 items.

rows.verbatim:
3.4.3 PIPELINES
QA EQUIPMENT ON THE DREDGE
Suction mouth depth chain/tape or calibrated pressure sensor
rows.normalized: For pipelines, Contractor must have QA equipment on the dredge: suction mouth depth chain/tape or calibrated pressure sensor.

rows.verbatim:
3.4.4 MECHANICAL DREDGES
QA EQUIPMENT ON THE DREDGE
Bucket depth chain/tape or calibrated pressure sensor
rows.normalized: For mechanical dredges, Contractor must have QA equipment on the dredge: bucket depth chain/tape or calibrated pressure sensor.

rows.verbatim:
3.4.5 SCOWS
QA EQUIPMENT ON THE DREDGE
Clear and accurate draft marks
Ullage tape
rows.normalized: For scows, Contractor must have QA equipment on the dredge: clear and accurate draft marks and ullage tape.

rows.verbatim: Transmit all data in XML message bundles (see DATA FORMAT).
rows.normalized: Contractor must transmit all hopper sensor data in XML message bundles.

rows.verbatim: If the plant is new to using DQM, please contact the DQM Center for a Plant Identifier.
rows.normalized: If the plant is new to using DQM, Contractor must contact the DQM Center for a Plant Identifier.

rows.verbatim: Load number for each plant will begin at number 1 at the start of the contract and will increment by one at the completion of each placement event.
rows.normalized: Contractor's load number for each plant must begin at 1 at contract start and increment by one at completion of each placement event.

rows.verbatim: Whenever possible, calculate the load number using sensors aboard the plant with a mathematically repeatable routine.
rows.normalized: Contractor must, whenever possible, calculate the load number using onboard sensors with a mathematically repeatable routine.

rows.verbatim: Make efforts to include logic that avoids false load number increments.
rows.normalized: Contractor must include logic that avoids false load number increments.

rows.verbatim: If manual increment of the load number is performed, pay extra attention to this value in the quality control process.
rows.normalized: If manual increment of the load number is performed, Contractor must pay extra attention to this value in the quality control process.

rows.verbatim: Report the date and time to the nearest second and referenced to Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) time based on a 24-hour format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).
rows.normalized: Contractor must report date and time to the nearest second, referenced to UTC, in 24-hour format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS).

rows.verbatim: The reported time must be the time reported by the Global Positioning System (GPS) in the National Marine Electronics Association (NMEA) data string.
rows.normalized: Contractor's reported time must be the time reported by the GPS in the NMEA data string.

rows.verbatim: Horizontal positions must be reported for all dragheads.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report horizontal positions for all dragheads.

rows.verbatim:
The COG
must be accurate to within 5 degrees and reported to the nearest whole degree with values
from 000 (true north) to 359 degrees referenced to a clockwise positive direction
convention.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report vessel course-over-ground (COG) accurate to within 5 degrees, to the nearest whole degree, using 000-359 clockwise convention.

rows.verbatim:
An “open” status must be reported as the bin starts to open, and
a “closed” status must be indicated only once the bin is fully closed.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report an 'open' hull status as the bin starts to open and a 'closed' status only once the bin is fully closed.

rows.verbatim:
For bins with
multiple doors or pockets, the “open”/”closed” status must correspond to the
compartment which is first to open and last to close.
rows.normalized: For bins with multiple doors or pockets, contractor's open/closed status must correspond to the compartment first to open and last to close.

rows.verbatim: Obtain location using a positioning system operating with a minimum accuracy level of 3-10 feet horizontal Circular Error Probable (CEP).
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain vessel horizontal location using a positioning system with minimum accuracy of 3-10 feet horizontal CEP.

rows.verbatim:
Report positions as
Latitude/Longitude World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84) in decimal degrees with
South Latitude and West Longitude values reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report positions as Lat/Long WGS 84 decimal degrees with South Latitude and West Longitude as negative values.

rows.verbatim:
Record vessel horizontal positioning as geographic coordinates of the vessel as indicated
by the location of the GPS antenna.
rows.normalized: Contractor must record vessel horizontal positioning as coordinates indicated by the GPS antenna location.

rows.verbatim:
Describe any offset calculations from the GPS
antenna(s) in the DPIP.
rows.normalized: Contractor must describe any GPS antenna offset calculations in the DPIP.

rows.verbatim:
Report positions as
Latitude/Longitude WGS 84 in decimal degrees with South Latitude and West Longitude
values reported as negative.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report draghead positions as Lat/Long WGS 84 decimal degrees with South Latitude and West Longitude as negative values.

rows.verbatim:
Record draghead horizontal positioning as geographic coordinates of the heel on the
centerline of the draghead(s).
rows.normalized: Contractor must record draghead horizontal positioning as coordinates of the heel on the draghead centerline.

rows.verbatim: Provide vessel course-over-ground (COG) using industry-standard equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide vessel COG using industry-standard equipment.

rows.verbatim:
Provide vessel speed-over-ground in knots using industry-standard equipment with a
minimum accuracy of 1 knot and resolution to the nearest 0.1 knot.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide vessel speed-over-ground in knots with minimum accuracy of 1 knot and resolution to 0.1 knot.

rows.verbatim: Provide vessel heading using industry-standard equipment.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide vessel heading using industry-standard equipment.

rows.verbatim: The only permissible values are “open” and “closed”.
rows.normalized: Hull status values are limited to "open" and "closed".

rows.verbatim:
Obtain the variation of the water level from the vertical datum for the river stage or tidal
gage using appropriate equipment to give the water level with an accuracy of ± 0.1 foot
and a resolution of 0.01 foot.
rows.normalized: Contractor must obtain water level variation from vertical datum with accuracy of ±0.1 ft and resolution of 0.01 ft.

rows.verbatim:
Enter vertical correction values above the project datum
with a positive sign and those below with a negative sign.
rows.normalized: Contractor must enter vertical correction values above project datum as positive and below as negative.

rows.verbatim:
Use datum and gage described
in the dredging specification and indicate in the state events when changing gages.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use the datum and gage described in the dredging specification and indicate gage changes in state events.

rows.verbatim:
Report all draft measurements in decimal feet with an accuracy of ± 0.1 ft and a
resolution of 0.01 ft relative to observed physical draft readings in calm water.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report all draft measurements in decimal feet with accuracy of ±0.1 ft and resolution of 0.01 ft.

rows.verbatim:
Values for
the forward draft and aft draft will be reported.
rows.normalized: Contractor will report values for forward draft and aft draft.

rows.verbatim:
The reported draft values are the averages
of the respective port and starboard physical draft mark readings.
rows.normalized: Reported draft values must be the averages of the respective port and starboard physical draft mark readings.

rows.verbatim:
Report vessel displacement in long tons to the nearest tenth, based on the most accurate
method available for the plant.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report vessel displacement in long tons to the nearest tenth using the most accurate available method.

rows.verbatim:
The minimum standard of accuracy for displacement is
interpolation from the displacement table, based on the average draft.
rows.normalized: Minimum standard of accuracy for displacement must be interpolation from the displacement table based on average draft.

rows.verbatim:
Report empty displacement in long tons to the nearest tenth, which is the lightship value
of the plant, or the weight of the vessel with no material in the bin, adjusted for fuel and
water consumption.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report empty displacement in long tons to the nearest tenth as defined (lightship value).

rows.verbatim:
Report forward and aft ullage distances in decimal feet with an accuracy of ± 0.1 ft and a
resolution of 0.01 ft relative to the ullage table reference point (typically the top of
coaming) at the forward and aft extents of the bin along the centerline.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report forward and aft ullage distances in decimal feet with accuracy of ±0.1 ft and resolution of 0.01 ft.

rows.verbatim:
Mount sensors to avoid discharge flume turbulence, foam, and any structure that could
produce sidelobe errors.
rows.normalized: Contractor must mount ullage sensors to avoid turbulence, foam, and sidelobe-error-causing structures.

rows.verbatim:
If sensors must be offset from the centerline of the bin, the
sensors should be offset to opposite sides of the vessel.
rows.normalized: If sensors must be offset from the bin centerline, they should be offset to opposite sides of the vessel.

rows.verbatim:
If more than one fore or one aft
sensor is used, place the sensors near the corners of the bin, and report the average value
of the fore sensors and the average value of the aft sensors.
rows.normalized: If more than one fore or aft sensor is used, contractor must place sensors near bin corners and report average values of fore and aft sensors.

rows.verbatim: Report draghead depths with an accuracy of ± 0.5 foot and a resolution to the nearest 0.1 foot as measured from the surface of the water with no tidal adjustments. Minimum accuracies are conditional to relatively calm water. The depth reported should be the bottom surface of the heel at the centerline of the draghead. Depths must be reported for all dragheads.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report draghead depths for all dragheads with accuracy of ±0.5 ft and resolution of 0.1 ft, measured from water surface with no tidal adjustments.

rows.verbatim: Use a density-metering device, calibrated according to the manufacturer’s specifications, to record the slurry density from each pump being used to move material in any phase of the dredging process to the nearest 0.001 grams per cubic centimeter (g/cc) with an accuracy of ± 0.01 g/cc. If the manufacturer does not specify a frequency of recalibration, conduct calibration prior to commencement of work. Densities must be reported for each draghead and pumpout path.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use a calibrated density-metering device to record slurry density to nearest 0.001 g/cc (±0.01 g/cc accuracy) for each pump, calibrate before work if manufacturer specifies no recalibration frequency, and report densities for each draghead and pumpout path.

rows.verbatim: Measure the revolutions per minute (RPM) of all pump impellers being used to move material in any phase of the dredging process. Dredges with multiple pumps per side must report RPM for the pump that best describes the dredging process. Pump RPM should be recorded to the nearest whole RPM.
rows.normalized: Contractor must measure RPM of all pump impellers and, for dredges with multiple pumps per side, report RPM for the pump best describing the dredging process.

rows.verbatim: Report bin volume in cubic yards to the nearest tenth, based on the most accurate method available for the dredge. The minimum standard of accuracy for bin volume is interpolation from the certified bin volume table, based on the average fore and aft ullage soundings.
rows.normalized: Contractor must report bin volume in cubic yards to the nearest tenth using the most accurate method, with minimum accuracy standard being interpolation from the certified bin volume table.

rows.verbatim: Report dragarm gimbal depths with an accuracy of ± 0.5 foot and a resolution to the nearest 0.1 foot as measured from the surface of the water with no tidal adjustments. Minimum accuracies are conditional to relatively calm water. The depth reported should be the center of the gimbal in both vertical and horizontal planes
rows.normalized: Contractor must report dragarm gimbal depths with accuracy of ±0.5 ft and resolution of 0.1 ft, measured from the water surface with no tidal adjustments.

rows.verbatim: Use a flow-metering device, calibrated according to the manufacturer’s specifications, to record the slurry velocity from each pump being used to move material in any phase of the dredging process to the nearest 0.01 feet per second (fps) with an accuracy of ± 0.5 fps. If the manufacturer does not specify a frequency of recalibration, conduct calibration SOLICITATION prior to commencement of work. Measure the slurry velocity in the same pipeline inside diameter as that used for the slurry density measurement. Velocities must be reported for each draghead and pumpout path.
rows.normalized: Contractor must use a calibrated flow-metering device to record slurry velocity to nearest 0.01 fps (±0.5 fps accuracy) for each pump, calibrate before work if needed, measure in the same pipeline diameter as density measurement, and report velocities for each draghead and pumpout path.

rows.verbatim: The draghead suction status must be reported if the dredge is equipped with valves designed to bypass the suction (i.e., suction not through the draghead). Contractor must use the status of the valves and the vessel’s configuration to determine a “true” value when suction is present at the draghead; and a “false” value when draghead suction is bypassed via the “turtle valves,” sea-chest” valves or other methods (with no suction at the draghead). The status must be reported as a Boolean value; The only permissible values are “true” and “false”.
rows.normalized: If the dredge has valves that bypass suction, contractor must report draghead suction status as a Boolean (true/false) value based on valve status and vessel configuration.

rows.verbatim:
Contractor must
use the status of the valves and the vessel’s configuration to determine a “true” value
when suction is present at the draghead; and a “false” value when draghead suction is
bypassed via the “turtle valves,” sea-chest” valves or other methods (with no suction at
the draghead).
rows.normalized: Contractor must use valve status and vessel configuration to determine true/false draghead suction values.

rows.verbatim:
The status must be reported as a Boolean value; The only permissible
values are “true” and “false”.

disposal vessel may be present within the SF-DODS SDZ at any time.

rows.verbatim:
The primary tracking system for recording ocean disposal operations shall
be disposal vessel- (e.g., scow- or hopper dredge-) based.
rows.normalized: The contractor's primary tracking system for ocean disposal operations must be vessel-based (scow- or hopper dredge-based).

rows.verbatim:
Each disposal
vessel shall have a primary navigation/tracking system functioning for
each disposal trip, calibrated for accuracy at a minimum at the beginning
of each ocean disposal project, that automatically and continually
indicates and records the following information throughout transportation
to, disposal at, and return from SF-DODS:
1. position of the disposal vessel, to a minimum accuracy of 3m (10
ft);
2. speed and heading of the disposal vessel;
3. fore and aft draft of the disposal vessel (sensors as near vessel
centerline as possible);
4. fore and aft bin height (top of dredged material load in the bin
or hopper) (sensors as near vessel centerline as possible);
5. time and location of each disposal event (e.g., the discharge
phase).
rows.normalized: Each disposal vessel must have a primary navigation/tracking system meeting listed data requirements (position, speed/heading, draft, bin height, time/location); 5 items in total.

rows.verbatim:
This system must record these data at a maximum 1-minute interval while
outside the SF-DODS disposal site boundary, and at a maximum 15-second
interval while inside the SF-DODS disposal site boundary and the SDZ.
rows.normalized: The tracking system must record data at least every 1 minute outside the SF-DODS boundary and every 15 seconds inside the boundary/SDZ.

rows.verbatim:
The
primary system must also include a real-time display, located in the
wheelhouse or otherwise visible to the helmsman, showing the position of
the disposal vessel relative to the boundaries of SF-DODS and its SDZ,
superimposed on the appropriate NOS chart so that the operator can confirm
proper position of the disposal vessel within the SDZ before discharging SOLICITATION
the dredged material.
rows.normalized: The primary tracking system must include a real-time display visible to the helmsman showing vessel position relative to SF-DODS/SDZ boundaries on an NOS chart.

the San Francisco District USACE, and NOAA's Gulf of the Farallones
National Marine Sanctuary.

The Web site must be searchable by disposal trip number and date, and at a
minimum for each disposal trip it must provide a visual display of: the
disposal vessel transit route to SF-DODS; the beginning and ending
locations of the disposal event; and the disposal vessel draft and load
level in the bin throughout the transit.

rows.verbatim:
Under all phases of the Project, hopper dredging will be conducted in accordance with the following hydraulic dredging standard practices included in the EA/EIR section 2.3.1.5 to avoid and minimize entrainment impacts to less than significant, including:
a. No dredging shall occur in water ranging from 0 to 5 parts per thousand salinity between December 1 and June 30.
b. USACE shall implement a worker education program for listed fish species that could be adversely impacted by dredging. The program shall include a presentation to all workers on biology, general behavior, distribution and habitat needs, sensitivity to human activities, legal protection status, and project-specific protective measures.
c. Pump priming, drag head clearing, and suction of water at the beginning and end of each hopper load shall be conducted within three feet of the seafloor.
d. Hopper drag head suction pumps shall be turned off when raising and lowering the drag arms from the seafloor.
e. The drag head, cutterheads, and pipeline intakes shall remain in contact with the seafloor during suction dredging.
f. The drag head water intake doors shall be kept closed to the maximum extent practicable in locations most vulnerable to entraining smelt. In circumstances when the doors need to be opened to alleviate clogging, the doors shall be opened incrementally (i.e., the doors shall be opened in small increments and tested to see if the clog is removed) to ensure that doors are not fully opened unnecessarily.
rows.normalized: USACE/dredging operations must follow six listed hydraulic dredging standard practices (salinity timing restriction, worker education program, seafloor clearance distances, pump shutoff procedures, contact maintenance, and intake door management) to minimize entrainment impacts.

rows.verbatim: This Order imposes mitigation measure BI-1 when implementing Phase 1 to reduce impacts to longfin smelt to less than significant (see Finding 17 and Provision 10, which imposes mitigation measure BI-1).
rows.normalized: USACE must implement mitigation measure BI-1 during Phase 1 to reduce longfin smelt impacts to less than significant.

1. The discharge of water, material, or wastes that is not otherwise authorized by the Order
is prohibited.
2. Dredging and disposal activities that create a condition of pollution or nuisance as
defined in section 13050(I) and (m) of the California Water Code are prohibited.
3. Overflow, leakage, or spilling of dredged sediment from barges, bins or dump scows
during transportation from the dredging site to the placement site is prohibited.

b. Biological Monitors (a lead delta smelt expert and three fisheries technician
