rows.verbatim:
At least 30 days prior to contract award, the USACE shall submit to the Commission’s Executive Director for review and approval the following information and
documentation:
a. Bathymetric Survey
A signed and most recent bathymetric pre-dredge survey depicting the location
of all areas authorized to be dredged, the proposed project depth including over-
dredge depth based on MLLW, the actual volume of sediment proposed to be
dredged based on the most recent survey, the results of sediment test analysis,
and the proposed disposal or placement site, and the approximate date of
project commencement.
b. Sediment Disposal and Placement
A written statement shall be submitted to the Commission’s Executive Director
with the following information: (1) the proposed disposal or placement site and
quantity of sediment to be disposed or placed, and dates within which the
disposal/placement episode is proposed; (2) if applicable, a discussion as to how
the volume proposed for disposal is consistent with in-Bay disposal site limits SOLICITATION
and/or disposal site allocations; (3) the results of chemical and biological testing of
sediment proposed for beneficial reuse or disposal; and (4) any changes to the IAA
for the individual project, if any.
c. Updated Information
Within 15 days after the contract award, the USACE shall submit the latest
bathymetric survey and written notification to the Commission that there are no
changes to the project; or any revisions to the volume of sediment proposed for
dredging, the disposal or placement site, and/or date of commencement from
the initial submission.
rows.normalized: USACE must submit to the Commission's Executive Director, at least 30 days prior to contract award, review/approval documentation including: a) bathymetric pre-dredge survey, b) written statement on sediment disposal/placement, c) updated information within 15 days after contract award; 3 items total.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall adhere to any special conditions contained in the episode approval letter.
rows.normalized: USACE must adhere to special conditions in the episode approval letter.

rows.verbatim:
a. Within 60 days of the completion of all dredging projects funded in the same
federal fiscal year, or by June 30th of the following calendar year, the USACE shall
submit a signed post-bathymetric surveys to the Commission showing the actual
area(s) and depths dredged including over-dredge depth based on MLLW; any
dredging that occurred outside the authorized area or depths; the total volume of
sediment dredged, the placement or disposal location(s), and the volume of
sediment placed at each site; and the dates the dredging occurred.
rows.normalized: USACE must submit signed post-bathymetric surveys to the Commission within 60 days of completing all dredging projects funded in the same fiscal year, or by June 30th of the following calendar year.

rows.verbatim:
If dredging is necessary outside the environmental work windows, the USACE shall
comply with the notification, monitoring, and conservation measures included in
the appropriate biological opinions and this Letter of Agreement.
rows.normalized: If USACE dredges outside environmental work windows, USACE must comply with notification, monitoring, and conservation measures in the biological opinions and this Letter of Agreement.

rows.verbatim:
No work inconsistent with the time and location limits contained in these figures
may be conducted without the written approval of an extension of time to
complete dredging and beneficial reuse and disposal by the Executive Director.
rows.normalized: USACE may not conduct work inconsistent with the time/location limits without written approval of a time extension from the Executive Director.

rows.verbatim:
Should the USACE obtain new or amended biological opinions that would change
the environmental work windows, the implementation of current biological
opinions, terms and conditions, or conservation measures, the USACE shall provide
them to the Commission for consideration.
rows.normalized: If USACE obtains new/amended biological opinions affecting work windows or conditions, USACE must provide them to the Commission for consideration.

rows.verbatim:

Agreement, the USACE shall work with the Commission staff to request and obtain
necessary amendments to this Letter of Agreement.
rows.normalized: If the Commission determines the new/amended biological opinion is inconsistent with the Letter of Agreement, USACE must work with Commission staff to obtain necessary amendments.

rows.verbatim:
No dredging (mechanical or hydraulic) is permitted from December 1 through May 31
upstream of, or within 1000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera
Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek
without the written approval of an extension of time to complete dredging and
beneficial reuse and disposal by the Executive Director.
rows.normalized: USACE may not dredge (mechanical or hydraulic) Dec 1-May 31 near specified tributary mouths without written approval of a time extension from the Executive Director.

rows.verbatim:
When circumstances necessitate that the USACE dredge before June 1st or after
November 30th anywhere in the Bay, to mitigate for impacts to Bay resources the
USACE shall place the sediment dredged after November 30th and before June 1st (or
August 1st for the Oakland Harbor Project) of any year at a designated beneficial reuse
site that will benefit fish habitat, consistent with the NMFS and USFWS amended LTMS
Programmatic Biological Opinions.
rows.normalized: If USACE dredges before June 1 or after November 30 anywhere in the Bay, USACE must place sediment dredged in that window at a designated beneficial reuse site benefiting fish habitat.

rows.verbatim:
the USACE shall limit the use of a hydraulic dredge as follows:
a. Suisun Channel
No hydraulic dredging shall occur in Suisun Channel and clamshell dredging shall
be limited to the months of August 1st through November 30th of any year.
rows.normalized: USACE must limit hydraulic dredge use; no hydraulic dredging in Suisun Channel and clamshell dredging limited to Aug 1-Nov 30; list continues with additional sub-items on next page.

rows.verbatim:
b. Pinole Shoal
Hydraulic dredging in Pinole Shoal Channel shall be limited to the work window
of August 1st through November 30th of any year to protect listed species and
specifically to minimize impacts to longfin smelt and migrating salmonids.
c. Richmond Inner and Outer, and Oakland Harbors
No hydraulic dredging shall occur at Richmond Outer Harbor from December 1st
to March 15th of any year to protect spawning herring, herring eggs, and larval
herring.
rows.normalized: Continuation of hydraulic dredge limits: Pinole Shoal Channel dredging limited to Aug 1-Nov 30; no hydraulic dredging at Richmond Outer Harbor Dec 1-Mar 15.

rows.verbatim:
Return water overflow from hopper-type hydraulic dredges shall be limited to no
longer than 15 minutes at the dredge site for each hopper load except in channels
where the shoaled material contains greater than 80 percent sand.
rows.normalized: USACE must limit return water overflow from hopper dredges to no more than 15 minutes per hopper load, except where shoaled material is >80% sand.

rows.verbatim: The training program shall be conducted prior to the use of a hydraulic dredge in San Francisco Bay.
rows.normalized: The worker training program must be conducted before a hydraulic dredge is used in San Francisco Bay, creating a dependency on dredge use.

rows.verbatim:
In addition, the following measures shall be implemented:
(1) Suction pumps shall be turned off when raising and lowering the drag arms
from the seafloor;
(2) The drag head or cutter head shall maintain contact with the seafloor during
dredging; and SOLICITATION
(3) Opening water intake doors on the drag head shall be minimized. When
necessary to alleviate clogging, the doors shall be opened incrementally, (i.e.,
the doors shall be opened in small increments and tested to see if the clog is
removed) to ensure that doors are not fully opened unnecessarily.
rows.normalized: During drag head operation, the dredge operator must implement measures including: (1) turning off suction pumps when raising/lowering drag arms, (2) maintaining drag head/cutter head contact with the seafloor during dredging, and (3) minimizing and incrementally opening water intake doors to avoid clogging; 3 measures in total.

rows.verbatim:
(1) By March 31, 2026, USACE shall submit a four-year entrainment monitoring plan,
acceptable to the Executive Director, that describes the collection and recording
of entrainment of native and listed fish and macroinvertebrate species.
rows.normalized: USACE must submit a four-year entrainment monitoring plan to the Executive Director by March 31, 2026.

The entrainment monitoring plan must include at minimum 7 elements: on-board monitoring, sampling all dredging phases, sampling both drag-arms, tide-related sampling, visual monitoring, presence/absence monitoring, and effectiveness evaluation procedures.

rows.verbatim:
(2) Annual monitoring reports containing the above-described information along
with any proposed updates to the monitoring plan shall be submitted to the
Commission by January 31st of the year following the dredging and monitoring
activities.
rows.normalized: USACE must submit annual monitoring reports to the Commission by January 31st of the year following dredging/monitoring activities.

rows.verbatim:
(3) The USACE shall report any special status species and natural communities
detected during the entrainment monitoring to the California Natural
Diversity Database (CNDDB).
rows.normalized: USACE must report special status species/natural communities detected during entrainment monitoring to the CNDDB.

rows.verbatim:
b. Alternative to Entrainment Monitoring
If the USACE identifies monitoring that is more beneficial to species of concern, it
may propose it to the Water Board and Commission staff for review and
approval by February 28th of the year in which its implementation is proposed.
rows.normalized: If USACE identifies more beneficial monitoring, it may propose it to the Water Board/Commission staff for review by February 28th of the implementation year.

rows.verbatim:
When the USACE uses a hydraulic dredge, it shall compensate for unavoidable take
of native and listed species via entrainment by:
a. purchasing longfin smelt mitigation credits at a resource agency-approved
habitat conservation bank; and/or
b. by beneficially reusing a volume of dredged sediment at a wetland restoration
project that benefits fish habitat.
rows.normalized: If USACE uses a hydraulic dredge, it must compensate for unavoidable take of native/listed species via entrainment by purchasing mitigation credits and/or beneficially reusing dredged sediment at a wetland restoration project.

rows.verbatim:
After implementing this mitigation requirement for three dredging seasons,
the USACE shall compile the amount of sediment dredged using hydraulic
dredges; the amount of water pumped through the system; the amount and
typed of fish and macro invertebrates entrained; the amount of sediment
beneficially reused; and the amount of wetlands (acres) restored as a result
of this mitigation requirement.
rows.normalized: After three dredging seasons of mitigation implementation, USACE must compile data on sediment dredged, water pumped, fish/invertebrates entrained, sediment reused, and wetlands restored.

rows.verbatim:
A three-year report shall be provided to the Commission by July 31, 2029 for review
and consideration in its next evaluation of any future USACE hydraulic Dredging
Program.
rows.normalized: A three-year report must be provided to the Commission by July 31, 2029.

rows.verbatim:
The USACE is required, as prescribed in the State and Federal Endangered Species Acts,
to consult with or obtain appropriate take authorization from the appropriate agencies
prior to undertaking dredging activities in San Francisco Bay which may affect any
federally or state listed species and is not
rows.normalized: USACE is required to consult with or obtain take authorization from appropriate agencies before dredging activities that may affect federally or state listed species.

rows.verbatim: The USACE shall use the appropriate protocols, as approved by the CDFW, NMFS, and/or USFWS, to ensure that project activities do not adversely affect rare, candidate, threatened and endangered species, as they are protected natural resources of San Francisco Bay and its tributaries.
rows.normalized: USACE shall use protocols approved by CDFW/NMFS/USFWS to ensure project activities do not adversely affect protected species.

rows.verbatim: Due to the presence of eelgrass beds in the vicinity of the Richmond and Oakland Harbor federal navigation channels, the USACE shall implement the USACE SF Bay Dredging Program Eelgrass Light Monitoring Plan 2024-2030 (Light Monitoring Plan), including turbidity minimization measures described in Table 1, Page 14 of the Light Monitoring Plan.

rows.normalized: USACE shall provide light monitoring report within 60 days of completion of post-dredge eelgrass survey.

rows.verbatim: Should the USACE determine it is necessary to alter the Light Monitoring Plan, it shall provide proposed changes to the Commission for review and approval 30 days prior to implementing changes.
rows.normalized: If USACE determines it necessary to alter the Light Monitoring Plan, USACE shall provide proposed changes to the Commission 30 days prior to implementation.

rows.normalized: USACE shall manage disposal volumes and locations in coordination with LTMS agencies to prevent material build-up.

rows.verbatim: If, at any time during the effective life of this Letter of Agreement, the Commission’s laws, Bay Plan policies, or regulations are changed and are in effect as enforceable policies of the Commission’s certified coastal management program under the federal Coastal Zone Management Act regarding dredging, dredged sediment disposal, and beneficial reuse, this Letter of Agreement shall become null and void unless the USACE agrees to amend its consistency determination, and agrees to new conditions to meet the new laws, policies, or regulations in a manner specified by or on behalf of the Commission, if appropriate.
rows.normalized: If Commission laws/policies/regulations change and become enforceable, the Agreement becomes null and void unless USACE agrees to amend its consistency determination and accept new conditions.

rows.normalized: USACE must implement the minimization measures for hydraulic dredging required under Special Condition II-H.3.

rows.verbatim: Therefore, the Commission has included Special Condition II-H.1. restrict hydraulic dredging during the herring spawning season in Richmond and Oakland federal navigation channels.
rows.normalized: USACE's hydraulic dredging is restricted during the herring spawning season in Richmond and Oakland federal navigation channels.

rows.verbatim: Special Condition II – C requires the USACE to provide an annual integrated alternative disposal site analysis to the Commission by March 31st of each year for review and approval.

rows.normalized: USACE is required by the Water Resources Development Act 2024 to beneficially reuse seventy percent of its dredged sediment nationally.

the USACE has stated that it will conduct dredging and dredged sediment disposal within the environmental work windows described in the LTMS
Management Plan and the requirements of the LTMS Programmatic Biological Opinions

At the same time, it commits to taking dredged sediment to beneficial reuse sites that provide fish habitat as
mitigation for work outside of the work windows, either in the same year or the
following dredge season.
rows.normalized: USACE commits to sending dredged sediment to beneficial reuse sites as mitigation for work outside work windows, in the same year or following dredge season.

requires the dredging within the work window and a process for evaluating time

that are important spawning habitat for Pacific herring, longfin and Delta smelt.

However, if a mitigation bank is not available, the USACE commits to an alternate
mitigation plan - beneficial reuse of dredged sediment.
rows.normalized: If a mitigation bank is not available, USACE commits to an alternate mitigation plan of beneficial reuse of dredged sediment.

requires an analysis of the effectiveness of the mitigation strategy be provided to the Commission after 3 years of program implementation to
assist in determining whether the strategy is working or should be revised in future
hydraulic Dredging Programming.
rows.normalized: Special Condition II-H.6 requires an analysis of mitigation strategy effectiveness be provided to the Commission after 3 years of program implementation.

Should either of these agencies require additional
mitigation, the USACE shall comply with those requirements.

rows.normalized: The proponent is required to place the portion of material dredged between December 1 and May 31 at the beneficial reuse site.

rows.verbatim: If a project is unable to place all of the material dredged outside the work window at a beneficial reuse site (e.g., due to equipment constraints or site availability), absent additional consultation, the project proponent will be required to provide an equivalent volume of material, deemed suitable for the purpose by DMMO, to a similar beneficial reuse site from a dredging project conducted inside the work window (June 1 to November 30) and not otherwise planned to go to a reuse site benefitting aquatic habitat.
rows.normalized: If a project cannot place all out-of-window material at a beneficial reuse site, the proponent must provide an equivalent DMMO-approved volume from an in-window project to a similar reuse site.

rows.verbatim: The placement of a like volume of dredged material at a beneficial reuse site must occur within 12 months of the end of the previous work window (i.e. November 30th).
rows.normalized: The proponent must complete placement of the equivalent volume of dredged material at a beneficial reuse site within 12 months of the prior work window's end (November 30).

rows.verbatim: Dredging at each project location will continue to be limited to the approved project depth plus over-depth.
rows.normalized: Contractor must limit dredging at each project location to the approved project depth plus over-depth.

rows.verbatim: No overflow or decant water will be allowed to be discharged from any barge, with the exception of spillage incidental to clamshell dredge operations, unless monitoring or relevant studies show the effects of such discharge are negligible on water quality.
rows.normalized: Contractor must not discharge overflow or decant water from any barge, except for incidental clamshell spillage, unless studies show negligible water-quality effects.

rows.verbatim: To reduce turbidity that may affect fish habitat, return water overflow from hopper-type suction dredges would continue to be limited to no longer than 15 minutes at the dredge site during any one excavation action (cut). Overflow would be unrestricted when dredged material is greater than 90 percent sand.
rows.normalized: Contractor must limit return water overflow from hopper-type suction dredges to 15 minutes per excavation cut, unless dredged material is over 90% sand.

rows.verbatim: Turbidity control and/or monitoring measures will be required per the provisions of the LTMS Programmatic EFH Agreement when dredging occurs in proximity to identified eelgrass zones.
rows.normalized: If dredging occurs near identified eelgrass zones, the contractor must apply turbidity control and/or monitoring measures per the LTMS Programmatic EFH Agreement.

rows.verbatim: Mitigation for any direct loss of eelgrass due to dredging will occur in consultation with NMFS, per the provisions of the LTMS Programmatic EFH Agreement.
rows.normalized: Contractor must mitigate any direct eelgrass loss from dredging in consultation with NMFS per the LTMS Programmatic EFH Agreement.

rows.verbatim: For hopper or pipeline dredging projects, a worker education program will be implemented for listed fish that could be adversely impacted by dredging. The program will include a presentation to all workers on biology, general behavior, distribution, habitat needs, sensitivity to human activities, legal protection status, and project-specific protective measures for each listed species.
rows.normalized: Contractor must implement a worker education program for hopper/pipeline dredging projects, including a presentation to all workers covering species biology, behavior, distribution, habitat needs, human-activity sensitivity, legal protection status, and project-specific protective measures.

rows.verbatim: Workers would also be provided with written materials containing this information.
rows.normalized: Contractor must provide workers with written materials containing the worker-education program information.

rows.verbatim: Draghead or pipeline pumps will only be turned on when the dragheads, cutterheads, or pipeline intakes are on the seafloor or within 3 feet of the seafloor when priming pumps.
rows.normalized: Contractor must only turn on draghead or pipeline pumps when intakes are on or within 3 feet of the seafloor (when priming).

rows.verbatim: Draghead, cutterheads, or pipeline intakes will be monitored so that they maintain positive contact with the seafloor during suction dredging.
rows.normalized: Contractor must monitor draghead, cutterhead, or pipeline intakes to maintain positive seafloor contact during suction dredging.

rows.verbatim: Hopper dredges will close, to the extent possible, the draghead water intake port’s doors in locations most vulnerable to entraining or entrapping listed fish.
rows.normalized: Contractor must close hopper dredge draghead intake port doors, to the extent possible, in locations most vulnerable to entraining/entrapping listed fish.

rows.verbatim: Planned LTMS dredging projects that are performed outside of the work windows for listed anadromous salmonids (June 1 through November 30) are required by the LTMS Program to placed dredged materials at a beneficial reuse site that will provide future aquatic habitat benefits for San Francisco Bay native species.
rows.normalized: Dredging projects performed outside the June 1-November 30 work window must place dredged materials at a beneficial reuse site providing future aquatic habitat benefits.

rows.verbatim:
Future dredging and disposal of dredged materials conducted under the LTMS Program and
addressed by this biological opinion must be conducted in compliance with the following
programmatic measures:
(1) The work window for dredging and disposal is June 1 through November 30.
(2) No dredging will be permitted from December 1 through May 31 upstream or within
1000 feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa River
Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek.
(3) Projects may plan work for the period outside the work window (December 1 through
May 31) provided the project mitigates for its impacts by placing dredged material at a
beneficial re-use site, such as tidal wetlands restoration site. If a project is unable to
place all material dredged outside the work window at a beneficial re-use site, the LTMS
Program measures allow for an equivalent volume of dredged material to be placed at a
beneficial re-use site from a project conducted within the work windows during the
following season. This exemption does not apply to dredge sites upstream or within 1000
feet bayward of the mouths of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare
Island Strait, Petaluma River, and Novato Creek.
(4) Projects that incur an unplanned and unavoidable need to complete a portion of an
ongoing dredging operation outside of the work window, the LTMS agencies may
approve up to 50,000 cubic yards of dredging and disposal per year for this purpose. This
exemption may apply to dredge sites upstream or within 1000 feet bayward of the mouths
of Larkspur/Corte Madera Creek, Napa River Channel/Mare Island Strait, Petaluma
River, and Novato Creek.
rows.normalized: Future dredging and disposal under the LTMS Program must comply with four programmatic measures: (1) work window of June 1-November 30, (2) no dredging Dec 1-May 31 near specified creek mouths, (3) conditional allowance to work outside the window if mitigation via beneficial re-use site occurs, with an exemption exception near specified creek mouths, (4) conditional agency approval of up to 50,000 cubic yards/year for unplanned work outside the window, with possible exemption near specified creek mouths; 4 measures in total.

rows.verbatim: Cutterhead dredges shall not be turned on until the suction dredge head is submerged in the sediment to minimize potential for entrainment of fish in the water column.
rows.normalized: Cutterhead pipeline dredges must not be turned on until the suction dredge head is submerged in sediment, to minimize fish entrainment.

rows.verbatim:
The Service has determined that the following Reasonable and Prudent Measure is necessary and
appropriate to minimize the effects of the proposed project on the species:
1. Adverse effects to longfin smelt DPS shall be minimized to the full extent possible.
rows.normalized: The party implementing the project shall minimize adverse effects to longfin smelt DPS to the full extent possible.

rows.verbatim:
a. The Corps, EPA, and/or applicant shall minimize the potential for harm or
mortality of longfin smelt DPS resulting from project related activities by
implementing the proposed project as described in the 1999 Programmatic
Biological Opinion, 2004 Amended Programmatic Biological Opinion, BA, and
summarized in the Description of the Proposed Action in this biological opinion.
rows.normalized: The Corps, EPA, and/or applicant shall minimize potential harm or mortality to longfin smelt DPS by implementing the project as described in specified biological opinions and the BA.

rows.verbatim:
b. The Corps, EPA and/or applicant shall ensure that their contractors or operators
comply with this biological opinion.
rows.normalized: The Corps, EPA and/or applicant shall ensure that their contractors or operators comply with this biological opinion.

rows.verbatim: The Service must be notified within 24 hours of the finding of any injured or dead listed species or any unanticipated damage to its habitat associated with the proposed project.
rows.normalized: Whoever discovers an injured or dead listed species, or unanticipated habitat damage from the project, must notify the Service within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim: Sightings of any listed or sensitive animal species shall be reported to the Service and the CNDDB (https://www.wildlife.ca.gov/Data/CNDDB/Submitting-Data).
rows.normalized: Sightings of any listed or sensitive animal species must be reported to the Service and the CNDDB.

rows.verbatim: Dead individuals must be sealed in a resealable plastic bag containing a paper with the date and time when the animal was found, the location where it was found, and the name of the person
rows.normalized: Dead individuals must be sealed in a resealable plastic bag with a paper noting the date/time found, location found, and finder's name.

rows.verbatim: Of special note, please ensure that the tracking data are being actively posted to the web, and that a project completion report is sent to EPA within 60 days of the completion of the work.
rows.normalized: A project completion report must be sent to EPA within 60 days of completion of the dredging work, and tracking data must be actively posted to the web

rows.verbatim:
“Surface Disposal Zone” or “SDZ” is the 600 m radius circle at the center of the overall
disposal site (latitude 37°39’N and longitude 123°29’W; NAD 83), within which the disposal
vessel must discharge all of the dredged material.
rows.normalized: The disposal vessel must discharge all dredged material within the 600 m radius Surface Disposal Zone (SDZ)
rows.section_ref: EPA SF-DODS Site Use Conditions A.5

rows.verbatim:
1. Prohibition on Leaking or Spilling During Transport: Dredged material shall not be leaked
or spilled from disposal vessels during transit to the SF-DODS. Transportation of dredged
material to the SF-DODS shall only be allowed when weather and sea state conditions will not
interfere with safe transportation and will not create risk of spillage, leak or other loss of
dredged material during transit. Disposal vessels must not be loaded beyond a level at which
dredged material would be expected to be spilled in transit under anticipated sea state
conditions, and in no case may disposal vessels be filled to more than 80 percent of the
vessel’s maximum bin or hopper volume. No disposal vessel trips shall be initiated when the
National Weather Service has issued a gale warning for local waters during the time period
necessary to complete dumping operations, or when wave heights are 16 feet or greater.
rows.normalized: Contractor's disposal vessels must not leak or spill dredged material in transit, must only transport under safe weather/sea conditions, must not be loaded beyond 80% of maximum bin/hopper volume, and must not initiate trips during gale warnings or 16-foot+ waves
rows.section_ref: EPA SF-DODS Site Use Conditions B.1

rows.verbatim:
2. Prohibition on Trash and Debris; use of Grizzly: Only dredged material determined in
advance by EPA and USACE to be suitable for ocean disposal may be discharged at SF-
DODS. Uncharacterized dredged material, vessels, trash, and other debris are prohibited from
being discharged at the site. In order to exclude large trash and debris (including rocks) from
being disposed at the site, before transport to SF-DODS all dredged material must be placed
into scows through a steel mesh or chain “grizzly” with openings of no more than 12 inches
by 12 inches. Material retained on the grizzly must be removed and disposed of separately.
EPA and USACE may on a case-by-case basis waive the requirement to use a grizzly if they
determine that trash and debris is unlikely to be present in the area to be dredged.
rows.normalized: Contractor must only discharge EPA/USACE-approved dredged material at SF-DODS, must pass all dredged material through a grizzly with openings no larger than 12x12 inches before transport, and must remove and separately dispose of retained material
rows.section_ref: EPA SF-DODS Site Use Conditions B.2

rows.verbatim:
3. Independent Inspector, and Scow Certification Checklist: Before any disposal vessel
departs for the SF-DODS, an independent quality control inspector (“independent” means not
a direct employee of the permittee or dredging contractor) must certify in writing that the
vessel is not over-loaded, and otherwise meets the conditions and requirements listed on an
EPA-approved Scow Certification Checklist that contains all of the substantive elements
found in the example contained in the most current SMMP Implementation Manual. EPA and
USACE must approve the proposed Scow Certification Checklist prior to the commencement
of ocean disposal operations. No ocean disposal trip may be initiated until both the towing
vessel captain and the independent inspector have signed all relevant entries on the Scow
Certification Checklist. The inspector shall provide a summary of any discrepancies or
inaccuracies on the Checklist in the permittee’s report to EPA and USACE for the relevant
month (see condition 10, below).
rows.normalized: Before any disposal vessel departs for SF-DODS, an independent inspector must certify in writing on an EPA-approved Scow Certification Checklist that the vessel is not overloaded and meets requirements; no trip may begin until both the towing vessel captain and inspector sign the checklist, and the inspector must report discrepancies in the permittee's monthly report
rows.section_ref: EPA SF-DODS Site Use Conditions B.3

rows.verbatim:
5. Surface Disposal Zone (SDZ): When dredged material is discharged within the SF-DODS, no
portion of the vessel from which the materials are released (e.g. hopper dredge or towed
barge) may be further than 1,960 feet (600 meters) from the center of the disposal site at
latitude 37°39’N; longitude 123°29’W. No more than one disposal vessel may be present
within the SF-DODS SDZ at any time.
rows.normalized: When discharging dredged material at SF-DODS, no part of the vessel may be more than 1,960 feet (600 m) from the site center, and no more than one disposal vessel may be present in the SDZ at a time
rows.section_ref: EPA SF-DODS Site Use Conditions B.5

rows.verbatim:
The primary tracking system for recording
ocean disposal operations shall be disposal vessel- (e.g., scow- or hopper dredge-) based.
rows.normalized: The contractor's primary tracking system for recording ocean disposal operations must be disposal vessel-based.
Each disposal vessel must have a calibrated primary navigation/tracking system recording position, speed/heading, draft, bin height, and time/location of disposal events on every trip.

rows.verbatim:
This system must record these data at a maximum 1-minute interval while outside the SF-
DODS disposal site boundary, and at a maximum 15-second interval while inside the SF-
DODS disposal site boundary and the SDZ.
rows.normalized: The tracking system must record data at max 1-minute intervals outside the SF-DODS boundary and max 15-second intervals inside the SF-DODS boundary/SDZ.

rows.verbatim:
The primary system must also include a real-time display, located in the wheelhouse or otherwise visible to the helmsman, showing the position
of the disposal vessel relative to the boundaries of SF-DODS and its SDZ, superimposed on
the appropriate NOS chart so that the operator can confirm proper position of the disposal
vessel within the SDZ before discharging the dredged material.
rows.normalized: The primary tracking system must include a real-time wheelhouse display showing vessel position relative to SF-DODS/SDZ boundaries on an NOS chart.

rows.verbatim:
Within 24 hours of the completion
of each disposal trip, data recorded from the primary disposal tracking system must be posted
by a third-party contractor to a World Wide Web (Internet) site accessible by EPA Region 9,
the San Francisco District USACE, and NOAA's Gulf of the Farallones National Marine
Sanctuary.
rows.normalized: A third-party contractor must post tracking data to a web site accessible to EPA, USACE, and NOAA within 24 hours of each disposal trip's completion.

rows.verbatim:
The Web site must be searchable by disposal trip number and date, and at a
minimum for each disposal trip it must provide a visual display of: the disposal vessel transit
route to SF-DODS; the beginning and ending locations of the disposal event; and the disposal
vessel draft and load level in the bin throughout the transit.
rows.normalized: The web site must be searchable by trip number/date and must display, at minimum, transit route, beginning/ending disposal locations, and vessel draft/load level for each trip.

rows.verbatim:
The third-party system must also generate and distribute “e-mail alerts”
regarding any degree of apparent dumping outside the Surface Disposal Zone of SF-DODS
(“mis-dumping”), and regarding any apparent substantial leakage/spillage or other loss of
material en route to SF-DODS.
rows.normalized: The third-party system must generate and distribute e-mail alerts for apparent mis-dumping and substantial leakage/spillage en route to SF-DODS.

rows.verbatim:
A functioning back-up navigation system, meeting the
minimum accuracy requirement listed above, must also be in place on the towing vessel (tug,
if any).
rows.normalized: A functioning back-up navigation system meeting the minimum accuracy requirement must be in place on the towing vessel, if any.

rows.verbatim:
If the primary (disposal vessel’s) navigation tracking system fails during transit, the
disposal trip may continue only so long as the back-up (towing vessel’s) navigation and
tracking system remains operational, by placing the towing vessel in such a location that, given the compass heading and tow cable length to the scow (“lay back”), the estimated scow position would be within the Surface Disposal Zone [i.e., within 1,960 feet (600 meters) of the center of the disposal site].
rows.normalized: If the primary navigation tracking system fails during transit, the disposal trip may only continue while the back-up towing vessel navigation system remains operational and the towing vessel is positioned so the estimated scow position stays within the Surface Disposal Zone.

rows.verbatim:
E-mail alerts for any disposal trip must SOLICITATION
be sent within 24 hours of the end of that trip to EPA Region 9, the San Francisco District
USACE, the relevant National Marine Sanctuary if the event triggering the alert occurred in
whole or in part within a Sanctuary boundary, and to other addressees as may be indicated by
EPA or USACE on a project-specific basis.
rows.normalized: The contractor must send e-mail alerts for any disposal trip within 24 hours of trip completion to EPA Region 9, USACE San Francisco District, the relevant National Marine Sanctuary (if applicable), and other addressees as indicated by EPA or USACE.

rows.verbatim:
In such cases the towing vessel’s position, and the tow cable
length and compass heading to the disposal vessel at the time of discharge, must be recorded
and reported.
rows.normalized: In back-up navigation cases, the towing vessel's position, tow cable length, and compass heading at time of discharge must be recorded and reported.

rows.verbatim:
Further disposal operations using a disposal vessel whose navigation tracking
system fails must cease until the primary disposal tracking system’s capabilities are restored.
rows.normalized: Disposal operations using a vessel with a failed navigation tracking system must cease until the primary system's capabilities are restored.

rows.verbatim:
In addition to the requirement in Special Condition 7 above for posting data on the Web, the
permittee shall maintain daily records for each
disposal trip to include: the Scow Certification Checklist; the amount of material dredged and
loaded into barges for disposal; the location (reach, stations, or dredging unit/sampling area)
from which the material in each barge was dredged; the weather report for and sea-state
conditions anticipated during the transit period; the time that each disposal vessel departs for,
arrives at and returns from the SF-DODS; the exact location and time of each disposal; and
the volume of material disposed at the SF-DODS during each disposal trip.
rows.normalized: The permittee must maintain daily records for each disposal trip including the Scow Certification Checklist, dredged material amounts, dredging location, weather/sea-state, transit times, disposal location/time, and disposal volume.

rows.verbatim:
The permittee
shall also maintain, for each ocean disposal trip, both electronic data and printouts from the
GPS-based primary disposal tracking system (or the backup navigation tracking system when
appropriate) showing transit routes, disposal vessel draft readings, disposal coordinates, and
the time and position of the disposal vessel when dumping was commenced and completed.
rows.normalized: The permittee must maintain electronic data and printouts from the GPS-based tracking system for each trip showing transit routes, draft readings, coordinates, and dumping start/end time and position.

rows.verbatim:
These daily records
shall be compiled at a minimum for each month during which ocean disposal operations occur,
and provided in reports, certified accurate by the permittee, to both
EPA and USACE by the 15th day of the following month.
rows.normalized: The permittee must compile daily records monthly and provide certified reports to EPA and USACE by the 15th day of the following month.

rows.verbatim:
For each ocean disposal trip, these
reports shall include the electronic tracking and disposal vessel draft data on electronic media
approved by EPA and USACE, as well as hard copy reproductions of the Scow Certification
Checklists and printouts listed above.
rows.normalized: Monthly reports must include electronic tracking/draft data on approved media plus hard copy Scow Certification Checklists and printouts for each trip.

rows.verbatim:
The monthly reports shall include a cover letter
describing any problems complying with the Ocean Disposal Special Conditions, the cause(s)
of the problems, any steps taken to rectify the problems, and whether the problems occurred
on subsequent disposal trips.
rows.normalized: Monthly reports must include a cover letter describing compliance problems, causes, corrective steps, and recurrence on subsequent trips.

rows.verbatim:
The permittee
shall report any anticipated, potential, or actual variances from compliance with these Ocean
Disposal Special Conditions, and any additional project-specific Special Conditions, to the
District Engineer and the Regional Administrator within 24 hours of discovering such a
situation.
rows.normalized: The permittee must report any variance from compliance with the Special Conditions to the District Engineer and Regional Administrator within 24 hours of discovery.

rows.verbatim:
If any of these compliance problems occur within the boundaries of a National
Marine Sanctuary, the permittee must also report any such situation to the relevant Sanctuary
office within 24 hours.
rows.normalized: If a compliance problem occurs within a National Marine Sanctuary boundary, the permittee must also report it to the relevant Sanctuary office within 24 hours.

rows.verbatim:
In addition, the permittee shall prepare and submit a detailed report of any such
compliance problems on a weekly basis by noon Monday, to the District Engineer and the
Regional Administrator.
rows.normalized: The permittee must prepare and submit a detailed weekly report of compliance problems by noon Monday to the District Engineer and Regional Administrator.

rows.verbatim:
These reports shall describe the cause(s) of the problems, any steps
taken to rectify the problems, and whether the problems occurred on subsequent disposal trips.
rows.normalized: Weekly compliance reports must describe the causes of problems, corrective steps taken, and recurrence on subsequent disposal trips.

rows.verbatim:
Within 60 days following the completion of ocean disposal
operations, the permittee shall submit to the District Engineer and Regional Administrator a
completion letter summarizing the total number of disposal trips and the overall volume (bin
as well as in-situ) of material disposed at SF-DODS for the project, and whether any of this
dredged material was excavated from outside the areas authorized for ocean disposal or was
dredged deeper than authorized by the permit.
rows.normalized: Within 60 days of completing ocean disposal operations, the permittee must submit a completion letter to the District Engineer and Regional Administrator summarizing trips, volume, and any excavation outside authorized areas/depths.

rows.verbatim:
Except in accordance with the July 9, 2015 programmatic
Biological Opinion and July 20, 2015 revised Incidental Take Statement (ITS) issued by the
National Marine Fisheries Service for projects conducted under the LTMS Program [including
ITS section 2.8.4(a)(iii)] all ocean disposal operations, including transport to and discharge at
SF-DODS, must cease by midnight of November 30, 2026. Otherwise, no ocean disposal
operations are authorized beginning December 1, 2026.
rows.normalized: All ocean disposal operations (transport and discharge) must cease by midnight November 30, 2026, unless covered by the specified Biological Opinion/ITS; otherwise no disposal is authorized beginning December 1, 2026.

rows.verbatim:
The permittee shall provide a copy of the Dredging
Operation Plan (DOP) to the EPA at least 48-hrs in advance of the dredging episode that will
involve ocean disposal; this may be conveyed via email.
rows.normalized: The permittee must provide a copy of the Dredging Operation Plan to EPA at least 48 hours in advance of any dredging episode involving ocean disposal.
